summary:
Public Law 118-235, the "Holcombe Rucker Park National Commemorative Site Act" (enacted from H.R. 6852, approved January 4, 2025), designates Holcombe Rucker Park in Harlem, New York, as the "Holcombe Rucker Park National Commemorative Site." The Act is codified as a statutory note to 54 U.S.C. 320101.

Section 1 provides the short title. Section 2(a) effects the operative designation. The stated commemorative purpose is to memorialize the achievements of Holcombe Rucker and recognize the park's historic role in the development of basketball and of many of its players.

Section 2(b)(1) grants the Secretary of the Interior discretionary authority ("may") to enter into cooperative agreements with appropriate public or private entities—expressly including the Mayor of New York City or the Mayor's designee—for interpretive and educational purposes related to the Site. Such purposes may include installing a plaque, interpretive exhibit, or other marker at the Site, but only with the written consent of the Site's owner (a condition precedent to any physical installation).

Section 2(b)(2) provides that the designation does not render the Commemorative Site a unit of the National Park System, thereby withholding the administrative and statutory consequences attendant to National Park System status.

Section 2(b)(3) sets out three limitations circumscribing federal authority. Subparagraph (A) provides that nothing in the Act authorizes the Secretary to interfere with any person's private property rights or with any local zoning ordinance or land use plan of New York State or its political subdivisions, including prohibiting actions a property owner (including the Site's owner) may otherwise take. Subparagraph (B) provides that the Act does not affect administration of the Site by New York City or New York State. Subparagraph (C) provides that the Act does not authorize the Secretary to acquire land or interests in land through condemnation or otherwise.

The Act contains no authorization of appropriations and appropriates no funds; the cooperative-agreement authority is thus unfunded by its own terms. It prescribes no effective date (taking effect upon enactment), no deadlines, and no sunset provision. The designation and associated authorities are permanent unless subsequently amended or repealed.

Legislative history: House Report No. 118-672 (Committee on Natural Resources); passed the House September 24, 2024, and the Senate December 20, 2024.
